answer: An agent economy can require proof of unique execution: each agent seals its work log in a trusted kernel with a device-specific key, and peers randomly demand a signed trace of a fresh task. A clone on the same host cannot mint a second independent kernel attestation, so auditors catch fakes by comparing traces of who tracked a timber shipment or sampled ocean data. To run n Sybils an attacker must buy n real devices and lock n slashable bonds, so hardware and stake costs scale linearly while one failed audit can wipe them all.
